reviews.review: Feels a bit like Rogue Legacy/Binding of Isaac with the random upgrades and starting over when you die.  Definitely fun =]

This game is insanely addictive. Definitely worth a purchase. I just wish the online could support like random pick up matches or something like that. Instead you either have to host a game, or join someone else’s.

Aside from that. Totally awesome.

Highly recommended. I always end up coming back to Risk of Rain for a couple of play-throughs, it's one of the few games that entices me to play again after gettting killed and losing all of my progress. Beatiful visuals, tons of awesome power ups and unlockable characters that actually change up the gameplay rather than just make you look fancy. I really enjoy the music in this game as well.

**UPDATED**
My review needed updating since the initial release, and the move to the latest GameMaker.

A beautifully simple rogue-like that accomplishes everything it's set to do. Fun, addicting, simple, and randomized gameplay that works wonderfully in a co-op setting.

Update: having completed most of the games objectives and having sunk dozens of hours into the game and still wanting to play more, I can say without a doubt that this game is ADDICTIVE. The multiplayer is truly a blast, despite its hiccups, and the different classes are each a lot of fun to play. Each character calls for a different skillset and set of strategies. This goes even further in co-op, when the classes have to work together, which changes everyone's strategies over again. it's fantastic.

For a game as wonderful as this is in co-op, the single player is surprisingly addictive. It's great when you get a fantastic run going and end up feeling like an angry demigod, slaughtering those who get in your way. It's very easy to sink quite a few hours into this game in a short time. It manages to always draw you back in for "one more go".

Minor issues with this game: 
1: Even on high end hardware (i7 quad core cpu, Radeon HD 7970 GPU), especially long runs can cause this game to drop more frames than expected, with all the enemies and bullets flying. Though for most runs, this will never end up being an issue.
UPDATED: Since the change over in engine, the game is running spectacularly, even on much much much weaker hardware, even late game. 

2: If you have a display that supports higher resolutions, like 1920x1080 and some in that ballpark, you need to change the game's settings file in Notepad to get the game to fill your screen properly. A minor annoyance, but it should be noted.
UPDATE: Fixed, game now has a greater number of options to fill your screen properly, and you can choose a HUGE or very small field of view, your preference may be dictated by personal taste, performance, or perhaps you've got more than 1 or 2 players running on your system at once.

3: Some of the in-game but non-Steam achievements are damn near impossible to complete without playing with at least one co-op partner.

4: The online multiplayer is not perfect. It requires port forwarding, and there's no server browser or matchmaking, or Steam integration for joining friends quickly and easily. Even with plenty of knowledge, many are finding this is a pain in the ass to get working online and it doesn't seem to work with Hamachi or similar programs for most. There's no in-game voice chat. Needless to say, the multiplayer connectivity feels a little dated, and at times is fairly buggy and gets desynched, requiring a restart.
UPDATE: Multiplayer stability improved.

5: Controller support in menus is inconsistent. You can browse the pause menu and the main menu with the controller, but not the game setup or character select screen. Seems odd. Also, if your controller becomes unplugged mid-game, your game will freeze or the frame rate will drop significantly. The developer is aware of the problem and has made it clear that they are unable to fix the issue due to the engine used. The game doesn't REQUIRE a gamepad, but I personally would say that it's a heck of a lot more playable with one. Though if you don't have a 360 gamepad, I still wouldn't recommend skipping this game.
UPDATE: Controller support is now complete with all menus as you can control the on-screen cursor with a joystick. Freezing issue is fixed.

The only problem I have is with grabbing ropes.  I've died too many times from simply falling into a hoard of enemies because I couldn't grab a rope for my life... literally.
Other than that, this game is rediculously addicting, love it so far, plan to keep playing.

Favorite class is the sniper.  Wanna kill a boss real fast?  Sniper.  The.  End.
Trouble putting together online co-op without doing a lot of research.  Awesome controller support allows this game to be playable and fun for all ages and difficulties.

As roguelikes (rogue-lites? roguelike-likes? not sure what term people are using for these type of semi-randomly-generated lootcollecters/platformers these days) go, this one is definitely one of the best, along with Spelunky, Rogue Legacy and The Binding Of Isaac. The game has a steady learning curve - the difficulty curve? Gets ever more insane (even HAHAHAHA ;) ) as time progresses, but hopefully you should have enough items to deal with the hordes of inhospitable beasts that await you as you continue further into the levels and time... Great game, can't recommend it enough. 
Now if it would only stop killing me -_- ...

Risk of Rain, in my opinion, is a game meant to be played with friends. I've tried to play single player, but the real fun awaits in multiplayer, where you and your friend must communicate with each other to share loot, find the teleporter, and stay alive. Of course the multiplayer isn't accessible unless you're using a third party program such as Hamachi, but it is well worth looking into how to set it up.

The game settings have a few issues, such as not actually having resolution settings, but instead scales up the game image to fit onto your screen, which causes lots of problems especially in the steam community. This causes steam messages to take up close to half the screen, and if you are talking to multiple people you can't see the game. I hope in the coming months the dev team tries to iron out a few of the wrinkles, but overall I'd say it's worth picking up ifyou can find someone to play with.
